clue.text: Message Margo sent back after Rae's made a fuss

indicators.note: after places the turned name behind the jumbled one
making a fuss stirs things up, so the name Rae is jumbled

parts.note: the name Rae, the possessive adding nothing

indicators.note: sent back tells us the name Margo is read from right to left

explanation.surface: A message comes after Rae kicked up a fuss about Margo being sent home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made a fuss' jumbles the name into AER; 'sent back' reverses the other name, and 'after' sets it behind. An aerogram is an airmail letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An airmail letter folded into its own envelope is a kind of written communication.

clue.text: Each gets a rook, bishop, knight, king, or queen

parts.words: rook, bishop, knight, king, or queen
parts.note: each of these is a chess piece

explanation.surface: Every player gets one of the chessmen.
explanation.walkthrough: The list names chessmen, each of them a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means for every one, individually.

clue.text: Flash automobile from which wave can be seen?

explanation.surface: A showy car from which the sea can be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rolls-Royce is nicknamed a Roller, a flashy car; a roller is also a long breaking sea swell.

clue.text: One in Greece shortly is one who is dead

indicators.note: in puts one word inside the short form of the country

parts.note: GR is an abbreviation for Greece
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in Greece is soon dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' signals the abbreviation GR for Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone done for, beyond saving, is informally said to be a dead person.

clue.text: Inattention of sailor with nous, so it's said

indicators.note: so it's said signals the words are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor, and nous is sense

explanation.surface: A sailor with common sense is said to be inattentive.
explanation.walkthrough: AB plus SENSE spoken sounds like the answer. Nous is British slang for practical good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An absence of mind is a lapse of attention, being elsewhere in thought.

clue.text: Start to ski all around on mountain tops — thus?

definitions.text: Start to ski all around on mountain tops — thus?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here of ski
around suggests moving the letters of all about into a new order
the tops of words are their initial letters, here of on and mountain

explanation.surface: A skier sets off and weaves all about the summits of a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' gives LAL; read whole, the clue describes the zigzag downhill race between gates.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue pictures a skier weaving between gates on a mountain course, which is that downhill event.

clue.text: See bird with a smile — in this opera a swan

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or look
a hen is a bird
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: Spot a bird smiling: in this opera there is a swan.
explanation.walkthrough: In Wagner's opera the knight arrives in a boat drawn by a swan.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's opera about the swan knight bears his name.

clue.text: Place for a ration a Liberal's gone

indicators.note: has gone means the letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: a ration is an allocation, a share
A plus L, the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician has left a place set aside for rations.
explanation.walkthrough: 's gone' removes A and L from ALLOCATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot or site is where something is situated.

clue.text: Made a big difference that it is dull red

parts.note: matte means dull, without shine
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something mattered because it was a dull red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that it is' only joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To be important or significant is to count for a lot.

clue.text: Lied about Head not moving a muscle

indicators.note: about suggests shuffling the letters of lied around

parts.note: a ness is a headland, a head jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Someone told a lie about a headteacher who never stirred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LIED into IDLE. A ness (as in Loch Ness's neighbour Ness Point) is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing nothing at all, lazing without stirring, is the state of inactivity meant.

clue.text: Tigress to chase round beginning to tussle

indicators.note: round asks for the letters to be turned about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as part of the mixture

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, from tussle

explanation.surface: A tigress sets off in pursuit, leading into a scuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges CHASE into SHECA; 'beginning to' adds the first letter of 'tussle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A female big cat of the striped kind is a tigress.

clue.text: A pile for Uriah, or so it is said

indicators.note: so it is said signals that we hear the name rather than see it spelt

parts.note: Uriah Heep is the creeping clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield

explanation.surface: A heap for Uriah, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep is the obsequious clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: A mound or stack of things is a pile.

clue.text: Removal of fences makes this a clean race

indicators.note: makes signals that the letters of clean race are worked into a new word

explanation.surface: Getting over every jump in show jumping counts as a faultless round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges CLEAN RACE; in show jumping, clearing every fence gives a clean round.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting rid of or getting over an obstacle is a clearing away of it.

clue.text: It's used in explosion I tremble to face!

definitions.text: It's used in explosion I tremble to face!

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the run explosion I tremble

explanation.surface: Someone trembles at facing a blast.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'explosion', the word 'I' and the start of 'tremble'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a component of gunpowder and so helps make a blast.

clue.text: Man, for example, is able? Not Jack!

indicators.note: Not tells us to leave the sailor out of the word able

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman

explanation.surface: A man is asked whether he is capable, Jack excepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland; 'Not' drops the able seaman from the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of an island.

clue.text: Accords we have broken, for slaughter it's not

indicators.note: broken means the letters of accords we are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: We have broken agreements, but this is not about killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges ACCORDS WE. The definition alludes to the cattle Hindus will not kill.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a holy bovine, an animal treated as untouchable and never killed.

clue.text: Intend to be free from guilt, hold bribe back

indicators.note: hold means one word wraps around the other

parts.note: someone free from guilt is pure

indicators.note: back tells us the word for a bribe is read the other way

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify, a bribe

explanation.surface: Someone means to stay innocent and refuse a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' and 'hold' work together: the reversed sop sits inside the word for innocent.
explanation.definitionFit: To aim or plan to do something is to have it as your goal.

clue.text: Be shortly sedated, perhaps, in this cot?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged another way
shortly means the word be is cut short

explanation.surface: Someone sedated is put to bed in a cot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts BE to B; 'perhaps' rearranges B plus SEDATED.
explanation.definitionFit: A cot is a small bed and this is the frame of a bed.

clue.text: Masks hold appeal for those who call by

indicators.note: hold means one word wraps around the other

parts.note: visors are face masks or shields
it means sex appeal, charm

explanation.surface: Masks are attractive to callers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as in an 'It girl' means sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Guests who drop in are callers.

clue.text: Diminutive girl in bad scene makes a show

indicators.note: in places the short name inside the jumbled word
bad suggests the word scene is spoilt into a new order

parts.note: Vi is a short form of the girl's name Violet

explanation.surface: A little girl in a nasty scene puts on a display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' gives ENCES, and 'in' places the short girl's name within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To display or reveal a feeling is to show it clearly.

clue.text: Well, pop is a drink that adds splash to your rye

definitions.text: a drink that adds splash to your rye

explanation.surface: Fizzy pop is the mixer that tops up a whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' is a filler; rye is American whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is fizzy pop, and soda water is the mixer splashed into whisky.

clue.text: Has in possession, wrongfully, "snow"

indicators.note: wrongfully suggests the letters of snow are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone holds snow illicitly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongfully' rearranges SNOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to hold it as your property.

clue.text: Alumnus has show that is dirty and blue

parts.note: an alumnus is an old boy, OB
a scene is a display, a show

explanation.surface: A former pupil puts on a show that is crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' means smutty, as in blue jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd, smutty material is indecent.

clue.text: Monkey is left or he's one of the crew

parts.note: a sai is a South American capuchin monkey
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monkey has been left behind, or else joined the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: The sai is a capuchin monkey, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaman is a member of a ship's company.

clue.text: Sounds out of your depth here on that you can count!

indicators.note: Sounds tells us the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: being out of your depth happens at the deep end of a pool

explanation.surface: Something that sounds like being out of your depth is reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deep end' spoken quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rely on someone is to count on them.

clue.text: In aspic exotic some flavour you'll get

indicators.note: In shows the letters sit inside the words aspic exotic

explanation.surface: An unusual savoury jelly gives a certain taste.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts after the A of 'aspic' and takes the E of 'exotic'.
explanation.definitionFit: A seasoning such as pepper or cinnamon is a flavouring.

clue.text: Cause to arouse, but aids sleep if upset

indicators.note: upset means the letters of aids sleep are knocked into disorder

explanation.surface: Something that helps you nod off wakes you if knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges AIDS SLEEP. The definition means to rouse someone's annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy or offend someone is to stir up their displeasure.

clue.text: Survive without Euro, the smallest amount

indicators.note: without, in its old sense of outside, means one word goes around the other

parts.note: to last is to survive

explanation.surface: Getting by without the euro is the minimum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking'; here it means outside, so LAST goes round E.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimum is the lowest possible quantity.

clue.text: Heath includes nothing from Beethoven's 3rd

indicators.note: includes means the plant name holds the other letter inside

parts.note: erica is the botanical name for heath or heather
zero, nothing, looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A man named Heath contains nothing of Beethoven's third.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heath' looks like the former prime minister and conductor Edward Heath; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer's Third Symphony is known as the heroic symphony.

clue.text: General you finally alleged is absurd

indicators.note: being absurd suggests the letters are thrown into nonsense order
finally picks the last letter of you

parts.note: taken as written as part of the mixture

explanation.surface: Something a person alleged at the end is ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives U from 'you', and 'is absurd' rearranges U plus ALLEGED.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles de Gaulle was a French army general and later president.

clue.text: Hell's brood could leave out of the will

parts.note: Dis is the Roman underworld, hell
one's own are one's family, one's brood

explanation.surface: The devil's offspring may be cut out of an inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's own' means one's family or offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: To reject a child and cut them from your estate is to renounce them.

clue.text: Worsted perhaps, but the opposite still

definitions.text: Worsted perhaps, but the opposite still

parts.words: Worsted perhaps, but the opposite still
parts.note: worsted means beaten and so does its opposite in form, built on better rather than worse, yet both mean defeated

explanation.surface: A woollen fabric is described as its own opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worsted' looks like the cloth; here it means beaten, from worst as a verb, and the better-based verb means the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat or surpass someone is to outdo them, just as to worst them is.
